analysis:
PORTFOLIO REVIEW: Four open positions, 61% deployed, $38K cash. LII is the standout winner at +12.35% — thesis intact, let it run. A is up modestly (+2.4%), fundamentals solid, hold. AMP and CI are both slightly underwater (-0.65%, -1.11%) but within normal noise; AMP is mixed/sideways below SMA50/200 with earnings in 23 days (watch closely), CI is barely above SMA200 with earnings 30 days out. Neither shows a thesis break — hold both with existing stops in place.

MARKET REGIME: SPY is in confirmed uptrend (+4.52% 20d slope) which favors staying invested, but the 5 consecutive stop-outs (-FICO, -IQV, -ADP, -MSFT, -ZBRA) are a clear warning that entries have been mistimed or too aggressive. Win rate 33% / PF 0.69x is below the break-even threshold — this demands selectivity, NOT more trades. The majority of the highest-quality screened candidates (WFC, PGR, SCHW, COF, DHR, MRSH, CI, MA) have earnings within 14-21 days, creating binary risk that makes new entries inadvisable for that cohort. ZBRA was a recent stop-out and is now 7.5% extended above SMA50 — skip. HWM at 87% 52w-range position is too extended per hard rules.

NEW TRADE RATIONALE: AON is the one name combining confirmed uptrend, basing in the lower third of its 52w range (29%), pristine fundamentals (ROE 46%, op margin 36%, $3.3B FCF, fwd P/E 15.3), and earnings far enough out (Jul 24, 24 days) to allow a proper setup to develop. ATR 2.8% gives a manageable stop around 5.5% below a limit entry. Risk/reward to 52w high is ~2.7x. Sizing keeps worst-case loss at ~1.5% of equity. This is a single high-conviction add; remaining cash stays reserved as a deliberate position given the recent losing streak and earnings-season noise.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $325.00, targeting a mild pullback from current $327.57. If price never pulls back and breaks above $335 cleanly on volume, reassess before chasing.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Aon is a near-oligopoly insurance broker with 46% ROE, 36% operating margins, $3.3B FCF, and a forward P/E of 15.3x — reasonable for this quality tier. Revenue growth of 6.5% is steady, EPS revisions are flat-to-positive. The business is highly recurring, non-cyclical, and generates predictable cash flows regardless of macro. TECHNICAL: Price is in a confirmed uptrend (basing), sitting at just 29% of its 52-week range, only 1.8% above SMA50, and 2.4% below SMA200 — this is the Stage 1-to-2 transition zone where risk/reward is historically best. SMA50 slope is turning flat-to-up (+0.3%). Entry at $325 places us at the lower edge of recent consolidation. Stop at $307 is 2x ATR below entry, giving the position room to breathe without violating Klaas's 15% drawdown ceiling.
trades.exit_plan: Exit on stop hit at $307. Thesis break: if op margins compress materially in earnings (Jul 24), or if price closes two consecutive days below SMA200 on elevated volume. Earnings-day risk acknowledged — if stock gaps down more than 8% post-earnings, exit immediately regardless of stop. On the upside, consider trimming 50% near $360 (recoup cost) and letting the remainder run toward $374 (52w high). Time stop: if price is flat or lower 60 days after entry with no progress toward SMA200 recapture, exit and redeploy.
